headline: 172 active wildfires are burning uncontained in the US today. The most serious is the Old Trails Fire in WA, threatening 23,677 structures.

active_threats.name: Old Trails
active_threats.narrative: The Old Trails Fire in Spokane County, WA has burned 3,226 acres and is 43% contained. NIFC's incident team reports **23,677 structures threatened**. 584 personnel are assigned. A forecast wind read wasn't available for this fire today.

active_threats.name: Little Giant
active_threats.narrative: The Little Giant Fire in Chelan County, WA has burned 111,428 acres and is 2% contained. NIFC's incident team reports **1,987 structures threatened**. 1,734 personnel are assigned. Winds are expected to stay comparatively light over the next 24 hours (gusts near 9 mph), which should limit further wind-driven spread for now. This is a sustained, terrain-channeled wind regime — the setup our WindNinja terrain downscaling is built to resolve. Forecast wind direction (NW, blowing toward the SE) favors pushing the fire toward Leavenworth city, 30 miles away.

emerging_conditions.narrative: A fire-weather pattern is developing over WY: Casper city, Rock Springs city, Green River city, Riverton city, and Rawlins city and 5 other communities sit under an active Red Flag Warning or Watch and SPC's **Elevated** fire-weather category. USGS fire-danger models put the local large-fire/spread probability as high as 13% in spots. No fire has been reported yet, but the combination of dry fuels and elevated fire weather is exactly the kind that produces a fast-moving run if an ignition occurs.
